cohort: The study included 82 women with preeclampsia and 169 healthy pregnant participants from Hangzhou, China.
finding: Higher concentrations of specific PFASs (PFOA, 6:2Cl-PFESA, PFUnDA) were associated with increased risks of preeclampsia (especially early-onset) and higher blood pressure, while higher PFOA and PFUnDA were also associated with increased odds of low birth weight and small for gestational age, although 4:2 FTS and ADONA showed inverse associations with LBW and SGA.
cross-section timing: Maternal serum samples were collected before delivery.
